svg.text: The T3 spread is mostly "who the subject is"
band-limited Pearson (0.1-0.6 Hz), 5-fold CV, 138 subjects x 10 tasks (1260 sessions)
subject identity explains 36.0 % of all score variance; the task only 8.6 % (additive two-way model, R² 0.446)
(a) T3 score vs the same subject’s median on the other 9 tasks
median score on the other nine tasks
sorted by the subject’s median over its tasks
rows read as bands, not speckle.
Split-half check (disjoint recordings): a subject’s median over the ODD tasks vs the EVEN tasks, Spearman +0.69 (Spearman-Brown reliability +0.82, n 137).
Caveat: one session per subject per task, so the person effect is inferred across tasks, not from repeated T3 recordings. Full detail: resp_t3_spread_sources.md
